accepted.name: users_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT "id" AS id,
       "first_name" AS first_name,
       "last_name" AS last_name,
       "email" AS email,
       "age" AS age,
       "gender" AS gender,
       "state" AS state,
       "street_address" AS street_address,
       "postal_code" AS postal_code,
       "city" AS city,
       "country" AS country,
       "latitude" AS latitude,
       "longitude" AS longitude,
       "traffic_source" AS traffic_source,
       "created_at" AS created_at
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS
accepted.description: Cleaned projection of THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.USERS exposing canonical user identifiers, profile attributes and created timestamp. Use this as the normalized users dimension for joins and user-level aggregates. | Use for: user demographics by geography/traffic_source; new users per period; churn or cohort analysis joined to events/orders

accepted.name: orders_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT "order_id" AS order_id,
       "user_id" AS user_id,
       "status" AS status,
       "gender" AS gender,
       "created_at" AS created_at,
       "returned_at" AS returned_at,
       "shipped_at" AS shipped_at,
       "delivered_at" AS delivered_at,
       "num_of_item" AS num_of_item
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS
accepted.description: Normalized projection of THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDERS exposing order-level identifiers, timestamps, status and basic measures. Use for order-level analytics and safe joins to ORDER_ITEMS or USERS. | Use for: orders over time; fulfillment latency (created -> shipped/delivered); returns rate at order level; join to ORDER_ITEMS for item-level metrics

accepted.name: order_items_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT "id" AS id,
       "order_id" AS order_id,
       "user_id" AS user_id,
       "product_id" AS product_id,
       "inventory_item_id" AS inventory_item_id,
       "status" AS status,
       "created_at" AS created_at,
       "shipped_at" AS shipped_at,
       "delivered_at" AS delivered_at,
       "returned_at" AS returned_at,
       "sale_price" AS sale_price
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS
grain: id -- one row per order item (order line)
accepted.description: Normalized projection of THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.ORDER_ITEMS exposing line-item identifiers, foreign keys, lifecycle timestamps, status and sale_price for item-level analysis. | Use for: item-level revenue, returns, and fulfillment; join to PRODUCTS or INVENTORY_ITEMS to enrich product attributes; per-item lifetime (created -> shipped/delivered/returned)

accepted.name: products_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT "id" AS id,
       "cost" AS cost,
       "category" AS category,
       "name" AS name,
       "brand" AS brand,
       "retail_price" AS retail_price,
       "department" AS department,
       "sku" AS sku,
       "distribution_center_id" AS distribution_center_id
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS
accepted.description: Projection of THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.PRODUCTS exposing product dimension attributes and pricing. Use for product-level joins and catalogue analytics. | Use for: product catalog reports; margin calculations when joined to order items (sale_price - cost); distribution center distribution of SKUs

accepted.name: inventory_items_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT "id" AS id,
       "product_id" AS product_id,
       "created_at" AS created_at,
       "sold_at" AS sold_at,
       "cost" AS cost,
       "product_category" AS product_category,
       "product_name" AS product_name,
       "product_brand" AS product_brand,
       "product_retail_price" AS product_retail_price,
       "product_department" AS product_department,
       "product_sku" AS product_sku,
       "product_distribution_center_id" AS product_distribution_center_id
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.INVENTORY_ITEMS
grain: id -- one row per physical inventory item
accepted.description: Projection of THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.INVENTORY_ITEMS exposing one row per physical inventory item with lifecycle timestamps and denormalized product attributes. Use for inventory turnover and sold-item-level analytics. | Use for: inventory turnover and time-to-sell; cost-of-goods-sold when linked to sold items; compare denormalized product attributes to PRODUCTS dimension

accepted.name: events_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT "id" AS id,
       "user_id" AS user_id,
       "sequence_number" AS sequence_number,
       "session_id" AS session_id,
       "created_at" AS created_at,
       "ip_address" AS ip_address,
       "city" AS city,
       "state" AS state,
       "postal_code" AS postal_code,
       "browser" AS browser,
       "traffic_source" AS traffic_source,
       "uri" AS uri,

FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.EVENTS
accepted.description: Normalized projection of THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.EVENTS exposing event-level rows for session and traffic analysis. | Use for: session funnels, pageview counts, traffic_source effectiveness; join events to users or orders to analyze pre-purchase behavior

accepted.name: distribution_centers_base
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT "id" AS id,
       "name" AS name,
       "latitude" AS latitude,
       "longitude" AS longitude
FROM THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.DISTRIBUTION_CENTERS
grain: id -- one row per distribution center
accepted.description: Projection of THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.THELOOK_ECOMMERCE.DISTRIBUTION_CENTERS exposing distribution center attributes for location-level joins and distance calculations. | Use for: geographic distribution of shipments or inventory; lookup for product/inventory distribution_center_id

accepted.name: order_items_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT oi.id AS id,
       oi.order_id AS order_id,
       oi.user_id AS user_id,
       oi.product_id AS product_id,
       oi.inventory_item_id AS inventory_item_id,
       oi.status AS status,
       oi.created_at AS created_at,
       oi.shipped_at AS shipped_at,
       oi.delivered_at AS delivered_at,
       oi.returned_at AS returned_at,
       oi.sale_price AS sale_price,
       o.status AS order_status,
       o.created_at AS order_created_at,
       p.name AS product_name,
       p.brand AS product_brand,
       p.category AS product_category,
       p.retail_price AS product_retail_price,
       p.cost AS product_cost,
       ii.product_sku AS inventory_sku,
       ii.product_distribution_center_id AS inventory_distribution_center_id
FROM order_items_base oi
LEFT JOIN orders_base o
  ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
LEFT JOIN products_base p
  ON oi.product_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN inventory_items_base ii
  ON oi.inventory_item_id = ii.id
accepted.description: Denormalized order items joined to orders, products and inventory items to expose order/context/product attributes in one row per order_item. Useful for revenue, margin and fulfillment analytics at item grain. | Use for: item-level revenue and margin (sale_price - product_cost); fulfillment latency and return rates by product/center; counts and totals by product_category/brand

accepted.name: orders_per_user_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT o.user_id AS user_id,
       COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS orders_count,
       SUM(o.num_of_item) AS items_ordered,
       MIN(o.created_at) AS first_order_at,
       MAX(o.created_at) AS last_order_at
FROM orders_base o
GROUP BY o.user_id
grain: user_id -- one row per user summarizing orders
accepted.description: Aggregated order-level measures per user: order count, total items ordered (sum num_of_item), first and last order timestamps. Use to profile customer activity and to join back to user cohorts. | Use for: customer RFM-style features; active users vs dormant users; join to users_base for demographics

accepted.name: product_sales_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT oi.product_id AS product_id,
       COUNT(1) AS items_sold,
       SUM(COALESCE(oi.sale_price,0)) AS total_sales,
       AVG(oi.sale_price) AS avg_sale_price
FROM order_items_base oi
GROUP BY oi.product_id
grain: product_id -- one row per product summarizing sales
accepted.description: Aggregated sales and quantity measures per product_id derived from order_items_base (sum of sale_price and count). Useful for top-seller lists and product performance monitoring. | Use for: top-selling products by revenue or units; price elasticity and average price monitoring; compare sales to product catalog retail_price

accepted.name: user_event_sessions_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT e.user_id AS user_id,
       e.session_id AS session_id,
       COUNT(1) AS events_in_session,
       MIN(e.created_at) AS session_start_at,
       MAX(e.created_at) AS session_end_at,
       COUNT(DISTINCT e.uri) AS distinct_uris
FROM events_base e
GROUP BY e.user_id, e.session_id
grain: user_id, session_id -- one row per user-session
accepted.description: Aggregated session-level metrics per user-session pairing: event count, first/last event timestamp, and distinct URIs visited. Useful for funnel and session analytics. | Use for: session duration and engagement; pre-purchase session characteristics when joined to orders

accepted.name: latest_event_per_session
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT id,
       user_id,
       session_id,
       sequence_number,
       created_at,
       ip_address,
       city,
       state,
       postal_code,
       browser,
       traffic_source,
       uri,
       event_type,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY session_id ORDER BY created_at DESC, sequence_number DESC) AS rn
FROM events_base
grain: session_id, rn -- multiple rows per session but rn=1 indicates latest event

semantic_filters.rn: use rn = 1 to select the latest event per session downstream

accepted.description: Latest event per session determined by created_at and sequence_number tie-breaker. Exposes a row per session with the last event; useful for session-level endpoint URI, last event_type and timestamps. | Use for: session endpoint page/URI analysis; identify last touch traffic_source before purchase

accepted.name: top_products_by_revenue_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT psa.product_id AS product_id,
       psa.items_sold AS items_sold,
       psa.total_sales AS total_sales,
       psa.avg_sale_price AS avg_sale_price,
       RANK() OVER (ORDER BY psa.total_sales DESC) AS revenue_rank
FROM product_sales_agg psa
grain: product_id -- one row per product with rank
accepted.description: Products ranked by total_sales within product_sales_agg. Exposes total_sales and a revenue_rank so downstream queries can filter rank <= K to get top-K products. | Use for: top-k product lists by revenue (use revenue_rank <= K); banding products into revenue percentiles

accepted.name: orders_fulfillment_latency
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT oi.id AS id,
       oi.order_id AS order_id,
       oi.created_at AS created_at,
       oi.shipped_at AS shipped_at,
       oi.delivered_at AS delivered_at,
       CASE WHEN oi.shipped_at IS NOT NULL AND oi.created_at IS NOT NULL THEN (oi.shipped_at - oi.created_at) ELSE NULL END AS time_to_ship,
       CASE WHEN oi.delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND oi.shipped_at IS NOT NULL THEN (oi.delivered_at - oi.shipped_at) ELSE NULL END AS time_ship_to_deliver,
       CASE WHEN oi.delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND oi.created_at IS NOT NULL THEN (oi.delivered_at - oi.created_at) ELSE NULL END AS time_to_deliver,
       AVG(CASE WHEN oi.delivered_at IS NOT NULL AND oi.created_at IS NOT NULL THEN (oi.delivered_at - oi.created_at) END) OVER (PARTITION BY oi.order_id) AS avg_time_to_deliver_per_order
FROM order_items_base oi
grain: id -- one row per order item
accepted.description: Calculate fulfillment latency metrics per order_item/order: shipment and delivery lag in seconds (or whatever epoch unit the timestamps use). Exposes derived latency columns for running/window analytics downstream. | Use for: fulfillment SLA and latency analysis; compare shipping performance by distribution center or product

accepted.name: user_lifecycle_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT u.id AS id,
       u.email AS email,
       u.age AS age,
       u.gender AS gender,
       u.country AS country,
       u.city AS city,
       u.traffic_source AS traffic_source,
       opa.orders_count AS orders_count,
       opa.items_ordered AS items_ordered,
       opa.first_order_at AS first_order_at,
       opa.last_order_at AS last_order_at
FROM users_base u
LEFT JOIN orders_per_user_agg opa
  ON u.id = opa.user_id
accepted.description: One-row-per-user summary joining users_base to orders_per_user_agg to produce demographic plus order-activity features useful for customer segmentation. | Use for: build user segments for marketing; lifetime activity cohorts and retention
